name: usage_kind_decode_counts
why: KIND_CD is decoded through CODES USAGE_KIND; the source holds an integer and the target holds the decoded string, so no canonicalization rule can compare them.
source_sql: SELECT NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(u.kind_cd) || ')') AS "kind", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM usage_events u LEFT JOIN codes c ON c.code_type = 'USAGE_KIND' AND c.code_val = u.kind_cd GROUP BY NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(u.kind_cd) || ')')

name: usage_units_by_tenant_and_kind
why: The decoded kind graded per tenant rather than only in aggregate, with the units sum PKG_RATING.compute_rating reads.
source_sql: SELECT u.tenant_id AS "tenantId", NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(u.kind_cd) || ')') AS "kind", COUNT(*) AS "n", SUM(u.units) AS "units" FROM usage_events u LEFT JOIN codes c ON c.code_type = 'USAGE_KIND' AND c.code_val = u.kind_cd GROUP BY u.tenant_id, NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(u.kind_cd) || ')')

name: usage_validator_domain
why: trg_usage_events_check becomes a $jsonSchema validator; this replays its two conditions (units > 0, kind in the enum) on both sides.
source_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS "violations" FROM usage_events u WHERE u.units <= 0 OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM codes c WHERE c.code_type = 'USAGE_KIND' AND c.code_val = u.kind_cd AND c.code_desc IN ('api', 'storage', 'compute'))

name: rating_period_totals
why: PKG_RATING's period roll-up: the embedded results[] must total what RATING_RESULTS totals per period.
source_sql: SELECT r.period_id AS "periodId", COUNT(*) AS "n", SUM(r.billable_units) AS "billableUnits" FROM rating_results r GROUP BY r.period_id
